finding.claim: MEDIUM (stored/indirect SSRF, Check 4). The user-supplied iconUrl is stored with no validation in PUT /profile and later fetched by the nightly sync job with an unrestricted GET. The attacker controls scheme, host and port, so they can make the server request internal hosts, RFC-1918 addresses or cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/). The response is not returned to the caller (ofByteArray, no visible use), so this is blind SSRF usable for internal port scanning and timing inference. Redirect risk depends on how the caller configures the HttpClient: java.net.http defaults to no redirects, but that cannot be verified from this file. The webhookUrl sink at line 21 is NOT a finding.
finding.source: Profile.update(String webhook, String icon) parameter `icon` (PUT /profile body field), assigned unvalidated to this.iconUrl at Profile.java:16

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives attacker-controlled `icon` from PUT /profile
this.iconUrl = icon; stored with no validation (the regex at line 12 only checks `webhook`)
URI.create(iconUrl) used as the request URI with no re-validation at fetch time
GET dispatched, body read as byte[]; blind from the caller's perspective

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check or host check exists on iconUrl in update() or sync(). The only validation in the file is the regex on `webhook` at line 12, which does not cover `icon`. No IP-resolution or private-range blocking. No in-repo CIDR egress config. Redirect handling is determined by the injected HttpClient, which is not visible here. Authentication on PUT /profile is not shown; if it requires a logged-in user, severity stays MEDIUM (blind, authenticated).

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the unvalidated `icon` (the regex at line 12 only checks `webhook`) and src/Profile.java:23 fetches URI.create(iconUrl) with GET, with no scheme or host guard anywhere in the repo, so the attacker controls the target (blind SSRF).
